types.embedding_query_text: Movie: A motion picture or film, typically produced for theatrical release or streaming. Also called Film, Motion Picture, Feature Film, Cinema. Examples: Spider-Man: Brand New Day, The Odyssey, Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie, The End of Oak Street.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Movie class directly matches the definition and examples of a motion picture film.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: MovieRentalStore
candidates.comment: A MovieRentalStore is a local business that offers movies for rent. Also called video rental store, film rental shop, DVD rental store. Examples: Blockbuster (historical), local video rental shop, Redbox kiosk. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is a venue for viewing movies.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Actor, Director. Examples: Anne Hathaway, Ewan McGregor, David Robert Mitchell, Christopher Nolan.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person class directly matches the definition and examples of an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: FilmStudio: A company that produces and distributes films. Also called Movie Studio, Production Company, Distributor. Examples: Sony Pictures, Paramount Pictures, A24.

chosen_type.label: FilmStudio
chosen_type.definition: A company that produces and distributes films.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a film production and distribution company; Organization is the closest parent.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: MovieRentalStore
candidates.comment: A MovieRentalStore is a local business that offers movies for rent. Also called video rental store, film rental shop, DVD rental store. Examples: Blockbuster (historical), local video rental shop, Redbox kiosk. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is a venue for viewing movies.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: MarketResearchFirm: An organization that conducts research to gather information about markets and consumers. Also called Research Company, Analytics Firm, Polling Company. Examples: Rentrak, CinemaScore, PostTrak.

chosen_type.label: MarketResearchFirm
chosen_type.definition: An organization that conducts research to gather information about markets and consumers.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a market research firm; Organization is the closest parent.

candidates.label: SearchResultsPage
candidates.comment: A web page displaying the results of a search query. Also called search results, SERP, query results page. Examples: Google search results page, Amazon product search results, a library catalog search page.

candidates.label: TouristInformationCenter
candidates.comment: A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point. Examples: a city visitor center, a national park information booth, a regional tourism office.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: AutoRental
candidates.comment: An AutoRental is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides vehicles for temporary hire. Also called car hire, vehicle rental agency, rent-a-car. Examples: Hertz, Enterprise Rent-A-Car, a local van rental service. Distinct from AutoDealer, which sells vehicles.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

types.embedding_query_text: ReviewAggregator: A website or service that collects and compiles reviews of products or services, such as movies or video games. Also called Review Site, Rating Platform, Critic Score Aggregator. Examples: Rotten Tomatoes.

chosen_type.label: ReviewAggregator
chosen_type.definition: A website or service that collects and compiles reviews of products or services.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an entity that aggregates reviews; Organization is the closest parent for a service/company.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: CriticReview
candidates.comment: A CriticReview is a professionally written and in-depth evaluation of a creative work, product, or service, published by a recognized reviewing source. Also called professional review, expert review, critical assessment, published critique. Examples: A movie review by a film critic, a restaurant review in a food guide, a book review in a literary magazine. Distinct from UserReview, which is a casual review written by a customer or general user.

candidates.label: ReviewAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent producing a balanced opinion about an object for an audience, resulting in a review. Also called assessing, evaluating, critiquing, giving feedback. Examples: a food critic writing about a new restaurant, a user submitting a product rating, a judge scoring a performance. Distinct from Review, which is the creative work itself, not the action of creating it.

candidates.label: AggregateRating
candidates.comment: An AggregateRating is a Rating that represents the average or summary of multiple individual ratings or reviews. Also called average rating, collective rating, summary score, overall rating. Examples: A product's 4.5-star rating based on 100 reviews, a movie's Rotten Tomatoes score, a restaurant's Yelp rating. Distinct from Rating, which is a single individual rating.

candidates.label: Review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called critique, appraisal, rating, feedback. Examples: a movie review on Rotten Tomatoes, a restaurant review on Yelp, a product review on Amazon, a book review in a newspaper.

types.embedding_query_text: Market: A place or system where goods and services are bought and sold, often referring to a specific industry or region. Also called Industry, Sector, Economy, Region. Examples: North American box office, overseas markets, box office, domestic.

chosen_type.label: EconomicMarket
chosen_type.definition: A system or region where goods and services are bought and sold, often referring to a specific industry.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an economic market or industry segment like 'box office'; Intangible is the closest parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: SellAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent exchanging goods or services for money with a buyer. Also called selling, vending, trading, transacting. Examples: a store selling a product to a customer, a person selling a used car, a company selling software licenses. Distinct from BuyAction, which is the reciprocal act from the buyer's perspective.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory. Also called Nation, State, Land. Examples: China.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Country class directly matches the definition and examples of a sovereign state or nation.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

types.embedding_query_text: GeographicScope: The extent of a geographical area or region. Also called Region, Territory, Area, Locality. Examples: globally.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org DefinedRegion class is the best fit for a general geographic area like 'globally', which is a non-administrative region.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: GeospatialGeometry
candidates.comment: GeospatialGeometry is an Intangible supertype of GeoShape, designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices. Also called spatial geometry, geographic feature. Examples: A GeoShape, a KML polygon, a GeoJSON object.

types.embedding_query_text: DateRange: A period of time spanning multiple dates. Also called Period, Timeframe, Interval, Span. Examples: this weekend, three weekends into its historic run, fifth weekend, first few days playing in China.

chosen_type.label: DateRange
chosen_type.definition: A period of time spanning multiple days, weeks, or months.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general date range; Intangible is the closest parent for an abstract time concept.

Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason

candidates.label: ServicePeriod

Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Season

Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day, month, and year. Also called Day, Calendar Date, Point in Time. Examples: Sunday, Monday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org DayOfWeek class is a perfect match for specific days of the week like 'Sunday' and 'Monday'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime

Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: A quantity of money or a financial amount. Also called Amount, Sum, Value, Price. Examples: $2 billion, $21 million, $20.5 million, $70 million.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MonetaryAmount class directly matches the definition and examples of a quantity of money.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: Rank: A position in a hierarchy or a list, indicating relative importance or performance. Also called Position, Standing, Order, Place. Examples: fourth-biggest domestic release ever, eighth movie ever, second-fastest, top five.

chosen_type.label: RankPosition
chosen_type.definition: A position in a hierarchy or a list, indicating relative importance or performance.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a rank or position in a list or hierarchy; Intangible is the closest parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: ItemList
candidates.comment: An ItemList is an intangible collection of items of any sort, often ordered or ranked. Also called list, collection, sequence, array. Examples: 'Top 10 Movies,' a shopping list, a playlist, a table of contents. Distinct from ListItem, which is a single entry within an ItemList.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration

Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

types.embedding_query_text: AudienceScore: A rating or score given by the general public or a specific audience group to a movie or other media. Also called Public Rating, Viewer Score, User Score. Examples: B CinemaScore, A CinemaScore.

chosen_type.label: Rating
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Rating class is the best fit for 'AudienceScore' examples like 'B CinemaScore', which are forms of evaluation.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: Rating
candidates.comment: A Rating is an Intangible representing an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars. Also called score, grade, review rating. Examples: a 4-star movie rating, a product's 8/10 score, a customer satisfaction rating of 5 out of 5, a restaurant's health inspection grade.

types.embedding_query_text: JobTitle: The name of a position held by an individual in an organization. Also called Position, Role, Occupation, Designation. Examples: head of marketplace trends.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org OrganizationRole class directly matches the definition and examples of a job title or position within an organization.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific number or amount of something. Also called Number, Amount, Count, Total. Examples: 3,446 locations, 3,545 theaters, 724 screens, 632 theaters.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Number data type is the most direct fit for raw numerical counts like '3,446 locations'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The part played by a person or thing in a particular situation or context. Also called Part, Function, Character. Examples: suburban parents.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Role class directly matches the definition and examples of a part played by a person or thing, such as 'suburban parents'.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

types.embedding_query_text: Source Examples: Studio Estimates.

chosen_type.label: InformationSource
chosen_type.definition: A place, person, or thing from which information or data can be obtained.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general source of information; Thing is the most general parent.

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

types.embedding_query_text: Group Examples: Critics, Audiences.

chosen_type.label: Audience
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Audience class is the best fit for groups of people like 'Critics' and 'Audiences'.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: CriticReview
candidates.comment: A CriticReview is a professionally written and in-depth evaluation of a creative work, product, or service, published by a recognized reviewing source. Also called professional review, expert review, critical assessment, published critique. Examples: A movie review by a film critic, a restaurant review in a food guide, a book review in a literary magazine. Distinct from UserReview, which is a casual review written by a customer or general user.

candidates.label: MedicalAudience
candidates.comment: An audience type representing target groups for medical web pages. Also called healthcare audience, patient demographic, medical readership. Examples: "patients", "healthcare professionals", "medical researchers", "general public interested in health".

types.embedding_query_text: RankValue Examples: 1, 2, 3, 4.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org QuantitativeValue class is the best fit for numerical values representing a rank, such as '1', '2', '3'.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
candidates.comment: A PostalCodeRangeSpecification is a StructuredValue indicating a range of postal codes, defined by a beginning and ending code. Also called zip code range, postcode boundary. Examples: 90210-90215, 00000-99999, a range of postal codes for a delivery zone.

types.embedding_query_text: MovieGenre Examples: Tamil-language romance, documentary.

chosen_type.label: MovieGenre
chosen_type.definition: A category or style of motion picture, characterized by conventions in narrative, theme, or aesthetic.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a movie genre as a distinct entity; Intangible is the closest parent for an abstract classification.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

types.embedding_query_text: RankDescription Examples: outside of the top 10, top of the charts, second place, third place.

chosen_type.label: RankDescription
chosen_type.definition: A descriptive phrase indicating a position or standing in a hierarchy or list.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a descriptive phrase for a rank; Intangible is the closest parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus

candidates.label: DrugPrescriptionStatus
candidates.comment: A DrugPrescriptionStatus is a MedicalEnumeration indicating whether a drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter. Also called medication availability, prescription requirement. Examples: PrescriptionOnly, OverTheCounter.

candidates.label: GameServerStatus
candidates.comment: A GameServerStatus is a StatusEnumeration representing the operational status of a game server. Also called server status, game server state. Examples: Online, Offline, Maintenance.
